ImageDescription.value: This small notebook was made in Czechoslovakia around the mid 1920s and was sold by the Hampshire Book Shop of Northampton, Massachusetts. The book was given to Charles A. Lindbergh in 1927 by Estelle Carpenter, the director of music for the San Francisco public schools, on behalf of herself and the students of the San Francisco schools. Her business card and a handwritten note appear near the back of the blank book: "Miss Estelle Carpenter / Director of Music, of / San Francisco / Public School. / and all Pupils / of San Francisco / Cal." Lindbergh loaned the book to the Missouri Historical Society in 1927, and he gave it to the Society in 1933.

Lindbergh in 1927 by Estelle Carpenter, the director of music for the San Francisco public schools, on behalf of herself and the students of the San Francisco schools.
